review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read `digitAt`, `BadAt` and the neighbouring lemmas in DigitAtToolkit.lean. I grepped the Egrs75 directory for how `BadAt` and `digitAt` are used. Neither definition has a `@[simp]` attribute or an unfolding lemma, and I found no `digitAt_def` or `badAt_iff` lemma. Every consumer unfolds the definitions by hand. I looked for simp loops and competing rules and found none, because the file has no simp lemmas of its own. This is a modest interface finding, not a defect that breaks anything. I did not run Lean. The proposed lemma and its exact form are untested.

findings.declaration: Egrs75.Probe.clearing_high (and its use of Egrs75.RepairPaperfaithful.BadAt / digitAt)
findings.excerpt:
unfold BadAt digitAt
  have := good_above_of_mem_window hq3 hlo hhi i hi
  omega
findings.problem: `BadAt` and `digitAt` are plain defs with no simp or unfolding lemma. Proofs about them must run `unfold BadAt digitAt` and then close the goal with `omega`. The helper `good_above_of_mem_window` is also stated with the raw expression `m / q ^ i % q`, not `digitAt q i m`. So the lemma and its only consumer do not match, and `clearing_high` needs a manual unfold plus `omega` to connect them. The same `unfold BadAt digitAt` step is repeated in SubtractBranch.lean, MuFinish.lean, BadPrefixRoute.lean and MoveDigits.lean. The toolkit has no canonical way to normalise `¬ BadAt q i n` into `digitAt q i n ≤ (q-1)/2`, or `digitAt` into `n / q ^ i % q`.
findings.proposed_change: In DigitAtToolkit.lean, next to the definitions, add an unfolding lemma such as `theorem badAt_iff : BadAt q i n ↔ (q-1)/2 < digitAt q i n := Iff.rfl`. Add `not_badAt_iff : ¬ BadAt q i n ↔ digitAt q i n ≤ (q-1)/2 := not_lt`, and possibly `digitAt_def : digitAt p i n = n / p ^ i % p := rfl`. Only the `BadAt` unfolding lemma should be `@[simp]`, because it rewrites to a smaller predicate in terms of `digitAt`. Keep `digitAt` itself irreducible-ish, to avoid unwanted expansion into `/` and `%`. Then restate `good_above_of_mem_window` with `digitAt q i m ≤ (q-1)/2`. The final step of `clearing_high` becomes `simpa [not_badAt_iff] using good_above_of_mem_window hq3 hlo hhi i hi`, or just `exact not_badAt_iff.mpr (good_above_of_mem_window ...)`. The `unfold`s elsewhere can go the same way.
findings.benefit: Every `¬ BadAt` goal reduces to a `digitAt` bound by one named rewrite. The helper's statement uses the same `digitAt` vocabulary as `lowDigits_iff_digitAt` and `digitAt_add_high`, so it can feed into them directly. Downstream proofs no longer unfold the definitions to raw `/` and `%` and rely on `omega`.

evidence.excerpt: def BadAt (q i n : ℕ) : Prop := (q - 1) / 2 < digitAt q i n
def digitAt (p i n : ℕ) : ℕ := n / p ^ i % p
